body.statement: For every \(p\ge2\), the one-root star construction contains a nonempty strict-inequality parameter region on which the pairwise rank matrix \(R\) is invariant under swapping the baseline with the root-intervention vertex. Consequently, no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).
body.justification: The obstruction shows that the correction needs entrywise support and marginal information, rather than a different scalar aggregation of the same ranks.
body.gap: Squires et al. use one rank score, but the literature does not establish an open-family impossibility for the entire class of equivariant rank-only selectors.
body.consumer: Method designers can rule out every rank-only baseline heuristic and focus on information-preserving summaries.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\geq 2\) and a member of the one-root star family in \(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\).  Vertex \(1\) is the unique root and, for each \(j\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\), the only edge into \(j\) is \(1\to j\), with coefficient \(b_j\neq0\).  By the definitions of \(A=I_p-B\) and \(a_j=A^{\top}e_j\),
\[
 a_1=e_1,
 \qquad
 a_j=e_j-b_je_1\quad (j=2,\ldots,p).
 \tag{1}
\]
All \(\omega_j\) and \(\tau_j\) are strictly positive.  Define
\[
 d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}.
\]
The star-family restriction gives \(d\neq0\), which is precisely effectiveness of the root intervention because \(\operatorname{Pa}(1)=\varnothing\).  Applying \(\texttt{lem:surgery-identity}\) to the root and using (1) gives
\[
 \Delta_1=d e_1e_1^{\top}.
 \tag{2}
\]
For a leaf \(j\geq2\), the same lemma and (1) give
\[
 \Delta_j
 =\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}
  -\omega_j^{-1}(e_j-b_je_1)(e_j-b_je_1)^{\top}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(\Delta_j\) is zero outside rows and columns \(\{1,j\}\), and its principal submatrix on those coordinates is
\[
 \left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
 -b_j^2/\omega_j & b_j/\omega_j\\
 b_j/\omega_j & \tau_j^{-1}-\omega_j^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Expanding the determinant in (4),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \det\!\left(\left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}\right)
 &= -\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j}
       \left(\frac1{\tau_j}-\frac1{\omega_j}\right)
    -\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j^2}\\
 &= -\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}<0,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{5}
\]
where the strict inequality uses \(b_j\neq0\), \(\omega_j>0\), and \(\tau_j>0\).  Consequently,
\[
 R_{0j}=\operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j)=2.
 \tag{6}
\]
Subtracting (2) from (4) and expanding once more yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \det\!\left(
   \left.(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 \right)
 &=\left(-\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j}-d\right)
      \left(\frac1{\tau_j}-\frac1{\omega_j}\right)
      -\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j^2}\\
 &=\frac{d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
The defining strict inequality \(d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2<0\) makes (7) nonzero.  Hence
\[
 R_{1j}=\operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_1)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)=2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Finally, (2) and \(d\neq0\) imply
\[
 R_{01}=\operatorname{rank}(K_1-K_0)=1.
 \tag{9}
\]

Let \(\sigma\) denote only the transposition of the two component labels \(0\) and \(1\); it fixes every leaf-component label.  Let \(P_\sigma\) be its permutation matrix on \(C\).  Equations (6) and (8) give \(R_{0j}=R_{1j}\) for every \(j\geq2\), equation (9) is symmetric in \(0,1\), entries indexed by two leaves are unchanged because \(\sigma\) fixes both indices, and every diagonal entry is zero.  These cases exhaust \(C\times C\), so
\[
 P_\sigma R P_\sigma^{\top}=R.
 \tag{10}
\]

The strict region is nonempty.  Indeed, set
\[
 \omega_k=1\quad(k\in V),\qquad
 \tau_1=2,\qquad
 \tau_j=1\quad(j=2,\ldots,p),\qquad
 b_j=1\quad(j=2,\ldots,p).
 \tag{11}
\]
Then all variances are positive, \(d=-1/2\neq0\), and for each leaf
\[
 d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2=-1<0.
 \tag{12}
\]
The root intervention is effective because \(\tau_1\neq\omega_1\); every leaf intervention is effective because its parent coefficient is nonzero, even though (11) permits \(\tau_j=\omega_j\).  The positivity conditions, \(d\neq0\), the conditions \(b_j\neq0\), and the finitely many inequalities in (12) all persist on a sufficiently small Euclidean neighborhood of (11).  Thus this is a nonempty relatively open parameter region of the fixed star graph contained in \(\mathcal M_p\) by \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).  The components are distinct throughout this region: (2) separates the root intervention from the baseline, (5) separates each leaf intervention from the baseline, (7) separates each leaf intervention from the root intervention, and, for distinct leaves \(j\neq k\), equation (3) gives \((\Delta_j)_{1j}=b_j/\omega_j\neq0\) but \((\Delta_k)_{1j}=0\).

Now let \(F\) be a component-permutation-equivariant rank-only baseline selector.  By \(\texttt{def:rank-compression}\), \(F\) is a map from rank matrices to component labels satisfying
\[
 F(P_\gamma R P_\gamma^{\top})=\gamma(F(R))
 \tag{13}
\]
for every permutation \(\gamma\) of \(C\).  Applying (13) with \(\gamma=\sigma\) and using (10),
\[
 F(R)=\sigma(F(R)).
 \tag{14}
\]
Neither \(0\) nor \(1\) is fixed by \(\sigma\).  Therefore (14) forces \(F(R)\in C\setminus\{0,1\}\); this conclusion remains valid when \(p=2\), when that fixed-point set consists of the single leaf label \(2\).  In particular \(F(R)\neq0\), whereas component \(0\) is the observational baseline.  Thus \(F\) fails at every point of the nonempty open region.  Since \(F\) was arbitrary, no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).

We finally record the archive-sound negative transfer without duplicating the embedding argument.  The sibling result \(\texttt{lem:squires-class-embedding}\) uses a reverse-topological latent-node bijection \(\rho\), satisfying \(u\to v\Rightarrow\rho(u)>\rho(v)\), and its permutation matrix \(Qe_j=e_{\rho(j)}\).  With \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=Q^{\top}\) and \(H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=Q\), that lemma verifies the Squires et al. assumptions and proves, with the context labels unchanged, that the published precision matrices satisfy \(\Theta_c=K_c\) for every \(c\in C\).  Hence it preserves every entry of \(R\), while the \(\sigma\) in (10)--(14) remains solely the component-label swap and is not used for latent relabeling.  Therefore the same open star family is a rank-preserving subfamily of the full Proposition-10 model class.  Any equivariant rank-only selector universally correct on that full class would restrict to one universally correct on this embedded family, contradicting (14).  This is only a negative transfer; it makes no positive recovery claim under latent mixing.
